### Prerequisites (listed separately)
1. retro ← care-cost (form **state**). Sentence "A retroactive release for months already paid is not issued until the award carries a rate adjustment that raises the annual pension for those months." — verbatim in retroactive_release_after_rate_increase_ab1baa5b (blocked side), plus a same-form restatement ("Equivalently: as long as the award carries no rate adjustment raising …"). In no other document (grep). Resolution basis: care_cost_rate_adjustment_29989a3f describes the write that brings a raising adjustment about in the records' words ("recomputes the annual Veterans Pension from an earlier effective date when the veteran reports recurring care costs"); records show only `b75602ee…` (5565 → 463/month = latest payment). Strength and connective ("not … until") intact.
2. care-cost ← statement (form **state**). Sentence "The new annual rate is fixed only after the award carries a benefit income statement from the veteran dated on the day his VA disability compensation stopped." — verbatim in care_cost_rate_adjustment_29989a3f, with a same-form restatement ("Put the other way …"). Not in benefit_income_statement_d2740470 or any other document. Resolution basis: benefit_income_statement_d2740470 describes the statement and its date; records show no such report and comp closed 2026-05-31. Strength and connective ("only after") intact.
`condition`, `resolved_by`, `fallback_reason` appear nowhere in prose.

Every normative sentence of the documents listed in source_to_kb, and of the base-policy and term documents (income_based_rate_rule, maximum_annual_rate_schedule, medical_expense_deduction_figures, countable_income_terms_by_category, reporting_income_changes, unreimbursed_medical_expense_reports, income_match_due_process, pension_and_disability_compensation_together, payment_calendar_and_account_terms, payment_schedule_and_returned_payments, housebound_aid_and_attendance_and_dependency, net_worth_limit_and_asset_transfers), traces to the three extended rules, their base policies, the variant parameters or the tool contracts. - "A release has an amount only when the new monthly rate exceeds the gross amount of the most recent monthly payment" (retroactive_release_amount) — the compute's `rate_raised` gate; entailed.
- "(a month ending on or after the date of receipt included)" (care_months_counted_in_care_adjustment) — the compute's day difference (negative ≤ 92); entailed.
- "Each part is taken in dollars and cents, the release part rounded to the cent" (benefit_income_statement_amount) — rounding the source pins; entailed.
- Factor documents that state their base as "the releases less any representative's fee taken out" (compensation_release_months_before_pension, compensation_release_deposit_timing_in_statement, compensation_release_share_for_pension_months) — the factor's own operand as the source pins it ("The share and that weight are applied to the releases less the fee taken out"); not a pointer.
- benefit_income_statement_amount: "A figure that is taken as reported is used at a factor of 1, that is, unchanged" — renders `no_adjustment_factor` of the baseline; neutral wording, no "unless / may apply". Observation only.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** Policy-side notes (do not change this verdict):
- N1 (origin of the KB-RUNTIME RED in runtime_context/…/0.md). The source rule dates the statement on the stop day ("The statement is dated as a change that began on the date the compensation award closed"; prerequisite sentence "dated on the day his VA disability compensation stopped") and ages its factors "before the statement", while its compute ages them to NOW (the filing day). The KB carries the prose faithfully (benefit_income_statement_d2740470 "Date of the statement"; "to the date of the statement" in compensation_release_deposit_timing_in_statement_3e8f14d7, social_security_figure_cost_of_living_raise_5a065f02, federal_civil_service_annuity_raise_in_statement_1d87717d), which entails the stop-day anchor; the scored value follows the compute. A prose-versus-compute inconsistency on the policy side; the documents make the prose reading more explicit but do not depart from it.
- N2. Statement recency (care-cost) and the declaration's prior-declaration test both read `income_source='other'`, which both user tools write; the prose distinguishes "benefit income statement" from "one-time declaration". No effect in this world.
- N3. In this world the state_due one-time declaration / net-worth policies are also arguably triggered (comp release deposited 2026-02-17 to a pensioner) but sit outside this tree; the GT does not act on them. Policy-side scope note.

## dependency_form

Hop marks from the blind answer: P1←P2 state-derived, P2←P3 state-derived; none pre-solved.
Corpus read for beyond-source statements:
- prerequisite sentences: carried only on the blocked side, in state form; restatements are same-form ("Equivalently …", "Put the other way …") and name no action, performer, tool or other problem.
- no document names another problem's tool (grep of the seven task-tool names: each occurs only in its own policy's document); no route, checklist, ordered multi-problem procedure or aggregated dependency table.
- care_cost_rate_adjustment "Not for a forward redetermination" and annual_rate_redetermination "Care costs reported" state the source's own rule sentences (each policy's rule), not a dependency the rendering added.
- titles/openings are general subjects ("Veterans Pension Care-Cost Rate Adjustment", "Veterans Pension Retroactive Release for Months Already Paid at a Lower Rate", "Veterans Pension Benefit Income Statement Certified by the Veteran"); none mirrors the task's situation.
- computation documents carry no "unless otherwise / adjustments may apply / certain veterans qualify" hint; factor documents state ladders as rules, say nothing about which tier a customer falls on, and do not point at the computation document.
- depended-on documents are reachable with the state's words (searches "rate adjustment raises annual pension …", "benefit income statement …" returned them first).

**PASS.**
